records.summary: Build API-connected waste receipt reporting software for permitted or licensed waste-receiving sites in Scotland and Northern Ireland. It would submit digital waste receipt reports to the government service when reporting becomes mandatory.
records.customer: Permitted or licensed waste-receiving sites in Scotland and Northern Ireland.

revenue_claims.claim: Approximately 12,000 permitted receiving sites in the UK first phase; not a Scotland/Northern Ireland customer count.
1,016 licensed sites for specified waste activities in Scotland in 2023; this excludes some site types and is not a phase-one customer count.
Approximately 550 NIEA-authorised waste facilities; not confirmed as a phase-one customer count.
IntelliWaste self-reports 1,000+ submissions and 3,000+ WTNs; undated usage claim, with no payer count.

records.paid_demand: Paid demand is unverified; no dated, independently verified paid-revenue event was found. Published competitor prices and self-reported usage do not establish payment.

competitors.name: Defra Report Receipt of Waste service
competitors.note: Official spreadsheet submission route; API-connected software is optional.

competitors.name: AnyWaste Free Core
competitors.note: Includes Defra submission.

competitors.name: LoadLog
competitors.price: Free for up to 5 WTNs monthly, then £12/month
competitors.note: Listed price; no sales evidence provided.

competitors.name: WasteMatrix
competitors.note: Listed price; no sales evidence provided.

competitors.name: Tipslip
competitors.price: £49/month for one site and £99/month for three
competitors.note: Listed prices; no sales evidence provided.

competitors.name: Byrne
competitors.note: Listed prices; no sales evidence provided.

competitors.name: First Mile Miley
competitors.note: Launch announcement dated 9 September 2026.

competitors.name: A-Gas RefHub
competitors.note: Launch announcement dated 1 October 2026.

rounds.plain: Defra's service accepts the required reports by spreadsheet under the same £26/year organisation account, so sites can report without buying an API connector.

risks: Paid demand and the eligible Scotland/Northern Ireland site count are unverified.
The spreadsheet route is expected to remain available until at least October 2027.
The free spreadsheet route and low-cost alternatives make a thin connector easy to replace.
Defra API access requires provider registration, testing, self-certification and production credentials; the guide describes 14 test scenarios.
Northern Ireland's legislative status adds date risk.
No operating evidence shows the workload can stay at or below 5 hours/week.
records.moat: No exclusive data or rules asset is demonstrated. Permit-specific mappings, weighbridge or system integrations, and trusted audit history could create value, but are potential assets rather than established advantages.

hours.value: Unverified; no evidence establishes 5 hours/week or less.
hours.note: Integration setup and customer-specific support could exceed the limit.

records.next_steps: Run a one-day no-code test with a clearly labelled pre-launch page and paid-pilot interest form in public waste-sector channels that allow vendor posts. Ask respondents for site nation, permit status, current system and willingness to pay for a specific integration; count qualified voluntary responses. Validate an unsupported incumbent-system integration before building.

records.summary: Build software that records waste movements and submits them to the digital waste tracking service for carriers, brokers and dealers. Mandatory digital tracking for waste collectors is planned from October 2027, after a public beta planned for spring 2027.
records.paid_demand: Paid demand is unverified. The sources name competitor offers and prices but provide no verified payment or revenue evidence.

competitors.name: AnyWaste Core
competitors.note: Waste-tracking product; launch reported in May 2026.

competitors.name: First Mile's Miley
competitors.note: Waste-tracking product; launch dated 9 September 2026.

competitors.name: WasteBolt
competitors.note: Incumbent price stated in the kill-check.

competitors.name: DEFRA Phase 2 Digital Waste Tracking service/API
competitors.note: Planned official service for carriers, brokers and dealers; no live official carrier operations product verified.

rounds.plain: Two competing waste-tracking products launched within the window: AnyWaste in May 2026 and First Mile's Miley on 9 September 2026.

risks: Final implementation details and paid demand are unverified.

records.summary: Build a lightweight tool that imports and validates waste-receiver spreadsheets, then turns them into compliant submissions to the digital waste tracking service. The government spreadsheet route is expected to remain available until at least October 2027.
records.paid_demand: Whether operators would pay for a spreadsheet-to-service bridge is unverified. No payment evidence is given.

competitors.name: DEFRA Report Receipt of Waste service
competitors.note: Provides spreadsheet submission for receivers as a temporary route, expected to remain until at least October 2027.

competitors.name: AnyWaste Core
competitors.note: Listed as a free incumbent.

competitors.name: WasteBolt
competitors.note: Listed incumbent price.

rounds.plain: DEFRA's Report Receipt of Waste service already offers spreadsheet submission for receivers, so operators can submit the same data without a separate bridge product.

risks: Whether operators would pay for the bridge is unverified.

records.summary: Build compliance software for vape manufacturers, importers and warehousekeepers to activate digital stamps, capture scan metadata and track movements. Digital stamps become the only stamps that may be affixed from 1 January 2027, and products outside duty suspension must carry a stamp by 1 April 2027.

revenue_claims.claim: HMRC estimated 200 manufacturers and up to 750 importers and warehousekeepers, while warning that the taxpayer population is uncertain.

£32 million excluding VAT estimated for the appointed stamp-scheme concession over five years plus an optional year; about one-third relates to non-profitable delivery costs. This is not realized software revenue.

VapeTax advertises £149/£500/£999 monthly plans, or annual equivalents of £119.20/£400/£799.20 monthly; its terms instead list Free/£249 Business/£1,499 Enterprise, so published pricing is inconsistent.

records.paid_demand: No verified customer payment or SaaS revenue for VapeTax or a proposed entrant was found. The listed prices and Cartor app installs do not establish paid sales.

competitors.name: Cartor SDAS
competitors.note: Official app for declaring and activating stamps; version 1.0 listed 17 September 2026 and version 1.0.1 on 8 October.

competitors.name: Cartor LOTE
competitors.note: Official app for recording and tracking movements; API pricing is unverified.

competitors.name: VapeTax
competitors.price: Homepage: £149/£500/£999 monthly, or annual equivalents of £119.20/£400/£799.20 monthly; terms: Free/£249 Business/£1,499 Enterprise
competitors.note: Published prices conflict; no verified sales evidence.

rounds.plain: HMRC's appointed supplier system already includes a Digital Activation System module and an EPCIS API for stamp scanning and traceability events.

risks: Cartor/SICPA already provides activation and movement-tracking workflows.
The LOTE API specification restricts commercial development based on its material without SICPA's express written permission; obtain written permission before building against it.
The regulated business population is limited and uncertain, and willingness to pay is unverified.
No evidence establishes 5 hours/week or less or a measured automation share.
records.moat: Weak at launch: the required product fields and duty rules are public, and the core workflows are already supplied by Cartor. Customer-approved ERP integrations, exception handling and validated product mappings could be useful, but depend on SICPA access and are unproven.

hours.value: Unverified; no operating record demonstrates 5 hours/week or less.
hours.note: This is a proposal without an operating cohort.

records.next_steps: Map Cartor's existing workflows and mock a missing ERP-to-LOTE reconciliation screen. Ask SICPA/Cartor for written commercial integration permission and offer a conditional paid pilot to verified incorporated businesses using generic corporate addresses; treat buyer commitment and written permission as required evidence before building.

records.summary: Build a self-serve tracker to help English landlords register properties as regions are called forward and retain registration evidence. The national service is scheduled to launch on 15 December 2026, roll out regionally over 12 months, and require actively letting landlords to register by 14 November 2027.
records.customer: English landlords, particularly those with multiple properties needing evidence preparation and reminders.

revenue_claims.claim: 5.03 million private-rented dwellings in England at 31 March 2025; a market-size proxy, not an exact count of properties covered by the rules.
2.88 million UK unincorporated landlords reporting rental income in 2024–25; excludes incorporated landlords and some people below Self Assessment reporting thresholds.

records.paid_demand: Revenue for this tracker feature is unverified. Lendlord publishes prices and feature descriptions, but no dated sales or payment data for the feature was found.

competitors.name: Government Register your rental property service
competitors.note: Provides registration and compliance evidence.

competitors.name: Lendlord Property Register / Compliance Hub
competitors.note: Registration-preparation feature; announced 13 October 2026.

competitors.name: Lendlord broader plans
competitors.note: Plan prices; not evidence of payment for the registration feature.

competitors.name: NRLA postcode deadline checker
competitors.note: Deadline checker.

competitors.name: Quarterday postcode checker
competitors.note: Publicly offered checker; launch date unverified.

competitors.name: Letcompliance
competitors.note: Adjacent tenancy-management software.

competitors.name: Letkept
competitors.note: Planned product collecting waitlist signups; asking price, not completed sales.

rounds.plain: The official registration service was scheduled for 15 December 2026 and was not live yet; no recent competing tracker was found in that check.
The official service already provides landlord registration and compliance evidence, and Lendlord announced a free registration-preparation tool.

risks: A direct, free competing registration tool and free deadline checkers exist.
The government service itself provides registration and compliance evidence, so willingness to pay for a separate tracker is unproven.
No verified product revenue, product-specific installs, automation share or 5-hour weekly workload was found.
Rules changes and annual renewals may create ongoing review and support work.
Electronic marketing to individual landlords and sole traders has consent restrictions described in the sources.
records.moat: Weak for a standalone tracker: rules, deadlines and fields are public, and a competitor offers the same preparation workflow for free. A maintained source-linked rules engine and broader compliance history could add practical value, but are not established advantages.

hours.value: Unverified; 5 hours/week or less is a target to measure in a paid pilot.
hours.note: Annual renewals and changing rules still require support and review.

budget.note: Refundable preorder test anchor based on Letkept's listed price; not established market pricing.

records.next_steps: Make a one-page mockup for multi-property evidence preparation and change/renewal history. Offer a sample evidence pack and refundable preorder at £8/property/month through moderator-approved public landlord communities or opt-in channels. Count paid commitments, not free signups; if nobody pays, do not build a standalone tracker.

records.summary: Build a document-to-data preparation tool for conveyancers handling reportable options, conditional contracts and pre-emption rights over registered land. From 6 April 2027, specified contractual control information must be submitted digitally to HM Land Registry through a regulated conveyancer, generally within 60 days for new or changed rights.
records.customer: Conveyancers handling reportable contractual control rights; developers and land promoters hold the reporting duty.

revenue_claims.claim: £3.7m a year in ongoing compliance costs across developers, land promoters and conveyancers, plus £4.5m one-off familiarisation costs; 2019 prices. These are policy cost estimates, not software spend or a serviceable market estimate.
£4.2m per annum in total business compliance costs, including £3.7m recurring costs and £4.5m one-off familiarisation costs, in 2019 prices.
3,119 firms reporting commercial-property work as of 20 October 2026; a broad, self-reported proxy, not a count of firms handling qualifying agreements.
HMLR had engaged around 31 firms and 48 legal professionals in service research by 17 September 2026; research participation, not purchase intent.

records.paid_demand: No evidence of willingness to pay for a third-party tool was found. The sources say law firms publish free preparation guidance; the number of qualifying agreements is unknown.

competitors.name: HM Land Registry contractual control digital service
competitors.note: Required submission channel; private beta planned for November 2026 and launch on 6 April 2027, with online mapping tools.

competitors.name: RegLand
competitors.note: Adjacent pre-validation for HM Land Registry applications; launched 26 May 2026.

competitors.name: ClearPathOS
competitors.note: Adjacent AI conveyancing and contract analysis; launch reported 24 August 2026.

competitors.name: Business Gateway-integrated case management suppliers
competitors.note: Existing suppliers; prices vary and are unverified.

rounds.plain: HMLR's official service was still under development, and the check found no evidence it already prepared data from documents or met another kill threshold.

The validation found no evidence anyone would pay and judged the small, uncertain market and HMLR-owned submission platform unable to meet the success and 5 hours/week limits. A regulated conveyancer must personally submit, limiting the tool to preparation.

risks: Agreement volumes are not estimated, and the reachable software market is only a fraction of the estimated compliance costs.
HMLR is building the submission service and mapping tools itself, leaving a limited preparation role for a third party.
A regulated conveyancer must personally submit; false or misleading information can be a criminal offence.
No willingness-to-pay evidence was found.
Owner hours are unverified and likely to exceed 5 hours/week due to security reviews, unusual clauses, format changes and partner sales.
records.moat: No established moat is stated. HMLR owns the submission platform and public rules; the sources say established vendors could add document-field extraction cheaply.

hours.note: The source cites legal-firm vetting, unusual clauses, format changes and partner sales as ongoing work.

records.next_steps: If reopened after HMLR publishes technical guidance, post a cited sample extraction page and paid-pilot form via opt-in conveyancing newsletters and ads. Count paid pilot commitments within two weeks; pass threshold is at least 3. This test was not run in v9.

The reported 12-month release gap is unverified.
